title: Perimeter and Area of 2D Shapes
summary: Calculate the perimeter and area of squares, rectangles, triangles, circles and composite shapes, convert between units of area, and investigate how changing dimensions changes the area.

notes.text: The **perimeter** of a shape is the total distance around its outside. It is a length, measured in mm, cm, m or km.

notes.caption: Perimeter formulae
rows: Add the lengths of all the sides

notes.text: The perimeter of a circle is called its **circumference**. The **radius** $r$ goes from the centre to the circle; the **diameter** $d$ goes right across through the centre, so $d = 2r$. For every circle, circumference $\div$ diameter is the same number, called **pi** ($\pi \approx 3{,}14$).

notes.caption: Circumference and area of a circle

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A circle has a radius of 7 cm. Calculate (a) its circumference and (b) its area. Use the $\pi$ key and round to two decimal places.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: $\pi r^2$ means $\pi \times r \times r$, not $(\pi r)^2$ and not $2\pi r$. Square the radius first. If you are given the diameter, halve it to get the radius before using $A = \pi r^2$.
**Area** is the amount of flat surface a shape covers. It is measured in **square units** such as $\text{mm}^2$, $\text{cm}^2$, $\text{m}^2$ or $\text{km}^2$.
The **height** of a triangle is the **perpendicular** distance from the base to the opposite vertex. It is not the length of a sloping side.

notes.caption: The height h (dashed) is perpendicular to the base. With base 8 cm and h = 5 cm, area = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm².

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem:
(a) Find the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm.
(b) A triangle has an area of $24\ \text{cm}^2$ and a base of 8 cm. Find its height.

notes.text: Because area has **two** dimensions, area conversions use the **square** of the length conversion. $1\ \text{m} = 100\ \text{cm}$, so $1\ \text{m}^2 = 100\ \text{cm} \times 100\ \text{cm} = 10\ 000\ \text{cm}^2$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: $1\ \text{m}^2$ is **not** $100\ \text{cm}^2$. Picture a square 1 m by 1 m: it holds 100 rows of 100 small squares of $1\ \text{cm}^2$.

notes.title: Worked example 3: tiling
notes.problem: A floor is 4,5 m by 3,2 m. How many square tiles of 30 cm by 30 cm are needed to cover it (assume no waste)?
steps: Work in cm: the floor is $450$ cm by $320$ cm, so its area is $144\ 000\ \text{cm}^2$.

notes.text: A **composite** shape is made of simpler shapes. Split it into rectangles, triangles or circles, find each area, then **add** (or subtract a missing piece).

notes.caption: An L-shaped room. The dashed rectangle (4 m by 5 m) is the part cut out of a 10 m by 8 m rectangle.

notes.title: Worked example 4: an L-shape
notes.problem: Find the area and the perimeter of the L-shaped room in the diagram.
steps: Area: big rectangle minus the cut-out: $10 \times 8 - 4 \times 5 = 80 - 20 = 60\ \text{m}^2$.
Check by splitting: top strip $10 \times 3 = 30$ plus bottom-left part $6 \times 5 = 30$, total $60\ \text{m}^2$ ✓
Perimeter: add all six sides: $10 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 8 = 36$ m.

notes.text: If you **double** every length of a shape, the perimeter doubles but the area is multiplied by $2^2 = 4$. If you triple every length, the area is multiplied by $3^2 = 9$. For example, a square of side 3 cm has area $9\ \text{cm}^2$; a square of side 6 cm has area $36\ \text{cm}^2$, which is 4 times as big.

items: Perimeter: distance around (units: cm, m). Area: surface covered (units: cm², m²).
Square: $P = 4s$, $A = s^2$. Rectangle: $P = 2(l + b)$, $A = lb$. Triangle: $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$ with $h$ perpendicular to $b$.
Split composite shapes into simple shapes; add or subtract their areas.
Multiplying all lengths by $k$ multiplies the area by $k^2$.

questions.prompt: Calculate the perimeter of a rectangle that is 12 cm long and 7 cm wide.
Calculate the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm.
Which formula gives the circumference of a circle with radius $r$?
questions.explanation: $C = 2\pi r$ (or $\pi d$). $\pi r^2$ is the area.

questions.prompt: Calculate the circumference of a circle with radius 7 cm. Use the $\pi$ key and round to two decimal places.
Calculate the area of a circle with radius 5 cm. Use the $\pi$ key and round to two decimal places.
A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. Calculate its area.
questions.explanation: Side $= 36 \div 4 = 9$ cm, so the area is $9^2 = 81\ \text{cm}^2$.

Round to two decimal places.

Semicircle: $\frac{1}{2}\pi (4)^2 = 25{,}13\ \text{m}^2$ ✓ (1)
Total $= 121{,}13\ \text{m}^2$ ✓ (1)
(b) Straight sides: $12 + 12 + 8 = 32$ m; curved part: $\frac{1}{2} \times 2\pi(4) = 12{,}57$ m ✓ (1)
